subject: math
cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume
description: Students use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure. Given a figure or description in which an unknown angle is expressed numerically or as an algebraic expression (e.g. $2x + 10$), students identify the governing relationship (angles summing to $90^\circ$, summing to $180^\circ$, equal vertical angles, or adjacent angles forming a known total), set up a linear equation, solve it, and report the requested angle measure in degrees.
subSkills: Identify complementary angles (two angles whose measures sum to $90^\circ$)
Identify supplementary angles (two angles whose measures sum to $180^\circ$), including a linear pair on a straight line
Identify vertical angles formed by two intersecting lines and recognize they are congruent
Identify adjacent angles that together compose a larger known angle (such as a right angle, straight angle, or full $360^\circ$ around a point)
Translate an angle relationship into a linear equation, including cases where one or both angles are algebraic expressions in $x$
Solve the resulting one- or multi-step linear equation for the unknown
Substitute the solved value back to compute the specific angle measure(s) the problem requests

problemArchetypes.name: Complementary angles
problemArchetypes.example: Two angles are complementary. One measures $34^\circ$. Write and solve an equation to find the other angle. ($x + 34 = 90$, so $x = 56^\circ$.)

problemArchetypes.name: Supplementary / linear pair
problemArchetypes.example: Angles $\angle ABD$ and $\angle DBC$ form a straight line. If $\angle ABD = 115^\circ$, find $\angle DBC$. ($x + 115 = 180$, so $x = 65^\circ$.)

problemArchetypes.name: Vertical angles
problemArchetypes.example: Two lines intersect. One angle measures $(3x - 5)^\circ$ and its vertical angle measures $70^\circ$. Solve for $x$. ($3x - 5 = 70$, so $x = 25$.)

problemArchetypes.name: Algebraic complementary or supplementary
problemArchetypes.example: Two supplementary angles measure $(2x + 10)^\circ$ and $(3x)^\circ$. Find $x$ and both angles. ($2x + 10 + 3x = 180$, so $x = 34$; angles are $78^\circ$ and $102^\circ$.)

problemArchetypes.name: Adjacent angles composing a known angle
problemArchetypes.example: Ray $BD$ lies inside right angle $\angle ABC$. If $\angle ABD = (2x)^\circ$ and $\angle DBC = (x + 15)^\circ$, find each angle. ($2x + x + 15 = 90$, so $x = 25$; angles are $50^\circ$ and $40^\circ$.)

problemArchetypes.name: Angles around a point
problemArchetypes.example: Three angles meet at a point and together make a full turn: $(x)^\circ$, $(2x)^\circ$, and $150^\circ$. Find $x$. ($x + 2x + 150 = 360$, so $x = 70$.)

problemArchetypes.name: Multi-step combined relationships
problemArchetypes.example: Two lines intersect; one of the four angles is $(4x + 8)^\circ$. Its supplement (the adjacent angle on the line) is $(6x - 28)^\circ$. Find $x$ and the measure of the larger vertical-angle pair. ($4x + 8 + 6x - 28 = 180$, so $x = 20$; angles are $88^\circ$ and $92^\circ$.)

Easy.description: A single relationship with one unknown that is a bare number or $x$. One-step equation; the relationship is named or obvious from the figure. No algebraic expressions beyond $x$ itself.
constraints: Exactly one relationship: complementary, supplementary, vertical, or one adjacent split
Unknown appears as $x$ or a single number, never as a multi-term expression
Solved in one step ($x + a = 90$, $x + a = 180$, or $x = a$ for vertical angles)
All given and resulting measures are positive integers in degrees

Medium.description: One relationship but at least one angle is a linear expression such as $2x + 10$ or $3x$. Requires writing a two-step linear equation, solving for $x$, then substituting back to report the requested angle measure.
constraints: At least one angle given as a linear expression in $x$ (e.g. $2x$, $x + 15$, $3x - 5$)
Equation requires two steps (combine like terms then isolate $x$)
Student must substitute $x$ back to produce the final angle measure
Integer solutions; angle measures remain valid (each strictly between $0^\circ$ and $180^\circ$)

Hard.description: Multi-step problems combining two relationships or requiring a chain of reasoning: e.g. variables on both sides, vertical angles set equal then a supplement found, or angles around a point with multiple algebraic terms. Student must select the correct relationship before setting up the equation.
constraints: Two or more relationships combined (e.g. vertical equality plus a linear pair), or angles around a point with multiple expressions
Equation has variable terms on both sides or three or more terms to combine
Final answer requires computing a second angle after solving for $x$
Relationship is not pre-named; student infers it from the figure description

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confuses complementary with supplementary, using $180^\circ$ when the angles are complementary (or $90^\circ$ when supplementary)
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Solves $x + 34 = 180$ to get $146^\circ$ for a complementary pair instead of $x + 34 = 90$ giving $56^\circ$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Thinks vertical angles are supplementary rather than equal, so subtracts from $180^\circ$
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Reports $180 - 70 = 110^\circ$ for an angle vertical to $70^\circ$ instead of $70^\circ$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Treats adjacent angles that compose a right angle as if they summed to $180^\circ$ (or those forming a straight line as if they summed to $90^\circ$)
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Uses the wrong total, e.g. solves $2x + (x+15) = 180$ for a right-angle split, yielding $x = 55$ instead of $x = 25$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Solves the equation for $x$ but forgets to substitute back, reporting the value of $x$ as the angle measure
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Gives the answer $34$ (the value of $x$) instead of the requested angle $78^\circ$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Sets up the relationship correctly but makes a sign or inverse-operation error when isolating $x$
Adds the two algebraic expressions but drops or mishandles the constant term when combining like terms
commonMisconceptions.distractor: From $2x + 10 + 3x = 180$ writes $5x = 180$ (ignoring the $+10$), getting $x = 36$ instead of $x = 34$
